Eligibility of VT Faculty/Staff for Graduate Degrees
Overview
Admission to the Graduate School is contingent upon receipt of a four-year baccalaureate degree (or three-year degree recognized by the Bologna process) from an accredited institution of higher education recognized by the U.S. Department of Education and listed in the Database of Accredited Postsecondary Institutions and Programs or an international equivalent. For applicants whose initial post-secondary degree is an integrated master’s degree or higher (i.e., no baccalaureate degree was awarded), the earned graduate degree is sufficient to satisfy the graduate admission contingency if earned from an institution of higher education accredited by a recognized U.S. institutional accrediting agency or an international equivalent, as verified from official transcripts. Additional requirements beyond those of the Graduate School vary across academic units. Prospective students are encouraged to review the requirements and conditions for admission before applying online. Degrees and their requirements are available at: https://catalog.vt.edu/. Students enrolled for graduate degrees at other universities are usually expected to complete their degree requirements prior to their matriculation at Virginia Tech.
Applications for admission should be submitted on-line at https://graduateschool.vt.edu/admissions/how-to-apply.html. If this is not possible, a printable application is also available.
Applications for admission are reviewed and evaluated by departmental or program-level graduate admission committees. Major factors considered in this evaluation are scholastic record, professional experience, letters of recommendation, and, as appropriate, scores on standardized tests. Individual departments and programs may have additional admission standards beyond those set by the Graduate School. Upon completing their review, departments or graduate programs submit their recommendation about admission to the Graduate School. The Graduate School finalizes and communicates the admission decision to applicants.
Credentials
Applicants must submit a copy of their transcript(s) with the online admission application. Each submitted transcript must show the institution name, the applicant’s name, a listing of courses completed, and the grade received in each course. Unofficial copies (student web portal printout, scanned student-issued hard copy, etc.) are acceptable for review by the department and Graduate School for admission consideration. Upon admission to and enrollment at Virginia Tech, Registrar's Office-issued transcript(s) from prior institution(s) showing degree conferral must be submitted to the Graduate School through sealed-envelope postal mailing or an eTranscript submission service. Failure to submit the final official transcript(s) during the first term of enrollment will result in a hold placed on the student’s academic record prohibiting enrollment in subsequent terms until the transcript(s) is received.
Departmental or program-level requirements
Letters of reference may be required by the graduate program or department and are submitted as part of the admission application.
Individual departments or graduate programs may require applicants to submit Graduate Record Examination (GRE) results. For applicants to the Pamplin College of Business, the Graduate Management Admissions Test (GMAT) may be required. If applicable, GRE or GMAT scores should be sent to Virginia Tech, using the Educational Testing Service Institution Code of 005859.
Please visit academic department websites for other departmental requirements such as resumes, vitas, portfolios, etc. All credentials submitted in support of an application become the property of the university.
International Applicants
Evidence of English Proficiency
International applicants may demonstrate English proficiency by submitting scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS). Minimum scores required for admission by the Graduate School:
TOEFL score of 90 on the internet-based test (iBT)
Sub-scores of at least 20 on each subtest (Listening, Speaking, Reading, and Writing)
TOEFL score of 577 on the paper-based test (PBT)
IELTS score of 6.5
Some departments have higher TOEFL or IELTS score requirements than those set by the Graduate School. Students who anticipate appointment as Graduate Teaching Assistants are expected to have scored 25 or greater on the TOEFL Speaking subtest. GTA appointment of a student scoring 20-24 on the Speaking subtest should be justified explicitly within the particular academic unit; appointment of a student scoring below 20 on the Speaking subtest requires justification with the Graduate School. For more details, see Testing Requirements.
Exceptions to English Proficiency Testing Requirement
International applicants who have graduated from an accredited university where English is the language of instruction or those who are U.S. permanent residents ("green card" holders) are exempt from demonstrating English proficiency.
Campus Locations
A program may be offered at a single campus or at multiple campuses. Students designate in their application for admission the campus location they wish to attend. Admission decisions specify the academic program, level, and campus to which a student is admitted. If a student wishes to attend a different campus than the campus they were admitted to, a Change of Campus Request form must be completed and approved by the academic program (and, for international students, by the Cranwell International Center), and the Graduate School. Campus designation impacts tuition and fee charges and the courses in which students may enroll.
International students in F-1 or J-1 visa status may pursue graduate degrees in Blacksburg or at the extended-campus in the Washington DC Metro Area. Questions regarding enrollment eligibility at the DC Metro Area location should be directed to the Cranwell International Center at international@vt.edu, 540-231-6527.
Admission Classifications
Students are admitted and classified in one of the following categories:
Regular Admission
Regular admission to a graduate degree is open to applicants whose grade point average (GPA) meets or exceeds the 3.00 required by the Graduate School for the last half of the credits earned for the undergraduate (bachelor’s) degree, and whose academic background meets the requirements of the admitting academic unit. A graduate degree, or at least 12 credits of post-baccalaureate graduate coursework taken while in graduate status with a GPA of at least 3.0 will supersede the undergraduate record in evaluating credentials for admission.
Provisional Admission (Master's only)
Provisional admission to a graduate degree is open to applicants whose GPA is below the 3.00 required by the Graduate School, but generally not lower than 2.75; who have other experience or qualifications that demonstrate potential to undertake graduate study; and whose admission is requested by the admitting academic unit. Provisionally admitted students are degree-seeking students with the condition that they must earn at least a 3.00 GPA for the first 12 graduate credits they attempt. If a 3.00 GPA is not earned in the first 12 credit hours attempted, the Graduate School will consult with the academic unit to determine whether the student should be allowed to continue for one additional semester on probationary status (see Academic Probation Due to Unsatisfactory Grades). Appropriate coursework taken while in Provisional status may be included on the Plan of Study for the student's graduate degree at the discretion of the student's Advisory Committee.
Non-degree Admission
Non-degree admission is open to applicants who qualify for admission to the Graduate School in Regular status (i.e., who have a 3.00 GPA or better for the last 60 credit hours of undergraduate study) but who do not wish to, or cannot be, listed as a degree candidate for one of the following reasons: (a) applicant does not currently desire to work toward a graduate degree; (b) applicant desires to transfer the credits for use toward a graduate degree at another institution; or (c) there currently is no higher degree available at the university than the one the applicant currently holds in the department or field of study.
The university places no limits on the total number of credits that may be taken while in Non-degree status. If the student is accepted into a degree program, the applicability of any courses taken while in Non-degree status will be determined when the Plan of Study for the degree is submitted. Graduate students in Non-degree status are not eligible for graduate assistantships.
Commonwealth Status
Commonwealth status is open to applicants who hold an earned bachelor’s or higher degree from a regionally accredited U.S. university. Examples of students who seek admission into Commonwealth status include those who (a) may qualify for regular admission but do not currently wish to work toward a graduate degree; (b) do not qualify for admission because of a poor undergraduate record and wish to improve their credentials; (c) need to update their academic credentials after several years of professional experience or (d) require graduate courses for professional certification. International students in F-1 or J-1 visa status are not eligible for Commonwealth status. However, some other visa statuses may allow non-degree enrollment (note that TOEFL or IELTS score requirements do apply). Students in Commonwealth status are not eligible for graduate assistantships.
Students are limited to 12 credits of course work while in this status, and they may not earn a graduate degree. Commonwealth status students who wish to enter a degree program must complete the Application for Admission for the degree program prior to the admission deadline for the desired semester.
If a student is accepted into a degree program, the applicability of any courses taken while in Commonwealth status, to the graduate degree, will be determined at the time when the Plan of Study for the degree is submitted.
Graduate Certificate Admission
Qualified students who wish to enter Virginia Tech to obtain a graduate certificate without being enrolled in a degree program may apply for admission to Graduate Certificate status online at https://graduateschool.vt.edu/admissions/how-to-apply.html.
Graduate students enrolled in a degree program may also add graduate certificates to their record. Such students should apply by completing the Application for Graduate Certificate Program form. Students pursuing a degree and a certificate simultaneously are classified in their degree program. All credits applied to the earning of a graduate certificate may be used in meeting degree requirements if they are appropriate for inclusion on the Plan of Study for the degree. No credits can be triple-counted.
The Office of University Scholarships and Financial Aid determines financial aid eligibility for students who enroll for graduate certificates only.
Visiting Graduate Student Admission
A graduate student in good standing at another regionally accredited university may be permitted to take graduate courses at Virginia Tech by submitting a Visiting Graduate Student Application form. Enrollment as a Visiting graduate student is limited to one calendar year or 18 credit hours.
Simultaneous Graduate Degrees
Students wishing to work toward two graduate degrees in different departments/programs at the same time should submit an Application for Simultaneous Graduate Degree form. See also Degree and Certificate Requirements, Simultaneous Graduate Degrees.
Readmission
When a student has not been registered for more than one calendar year, an Application for Readmission is required, whether or not the student has been on a formal Leave of Absence. The readmission process requires a review of both the student's progress and of the Plan of Study to determine what changes, justification of previous course work, committee updates, or other conditions may be required for readmission to the degree (the forms required for these processes are at: https://graduateschool.vt.edu/forms.html). For a full description of the readmission process, visit https://graduateschool.vt.edu/admissions/how-to-apply/readmission.html.
Virginia Tech Undergraduates Taking Graduate Courses
Seniors
Undergraduate students in their senior year with a 3.0 or better GPA may enroll in 5000-level courses that satisfy undergraduate degree requirements within their department with the permission of the course instructor and the Department Head. Should the student become a graduate student, these courses may not be used on the Plan of Study for a graduate degree.
Dual Student Status
Seniors in a bachelor's degree program who have a GPA of 3.0 or better may be eligible for Dual status during the final semester of their undergraduate degree. To obtain this status, students must file an application for the master's degree and the Accelerated Undergraduate/Graduate Degree and Course Designation Request (for obtaining Dual Status). The department reviews the student for master's acceptance and, if this is recommended, indicates that the student will be accepted for Dual status for the final semester of the undergraduate degree. This acceptance must occur prior to the final semester of the undergraduate degree. Graduate coursework taken during the semester of Dual registration may only be designated for use in the graduate degree when it is not used to meet bachelor's degree requirements (i.e., each course taken during the final semester is specified as being either for the bachelor's or the master's degree). A grade of B or higher must be earned in each Dual course to be placed on the graduate transcript.
Combined Student Status (Architecture Only)
This status is reserved for qualified students in the bachelor of architecture program who: (a) are within 24 semester hours of graduation; (b) are proceeding toward the two-year master's program in architecture; and (c) have at least a 3.0 GPA for the last two years (60 credit hours) of undergraduate studies. Combined students are permitted to take graduate courses.
Accelerated Undergraduate/Graduate Degree Programs
Some graduate programs offer one or more accelerated undergraduate/graduate degree programs. Minimum requirements to qualify include:
Students must be accepted into the program prior to the start of the semester in which they would enroll in courses to be used in the accelerated program.
Students must be in the last 12 months of their undergraduate degree.
Students must have a minimum GPA of 3.3 at the time of acceptance to the program.
Once completion of the undergraduate degree has been verified, students accepted into the accelerated program will be classified as Regular graduate students.
A maximum of 12 credits of graded coursework may be used in the accelerated program.
No more than 6 of the double-counted credits may be at the 4000 level; all others must be offered for graduate credit.
A grade of B or higher must be earned in each course to be double counted.
For a list of approved accelerated undergraduate/graduate programs, see https://graduateschool.vt.edu/admissions/accelerated_masters_programs/accelerated_ug-gr_program_listing.html.
Eligibility of VT Faculty/Staff for Graduate Degrees
Teaching and research faculty of the rank of assistant professor or above may not become candidates for a degree or be awarded graduate degrees from this university. The Provost's Office may be requested to waive this policy for an individual following a successful appeal to the Commission on Faculty Affairs.
Staff and administrative/professional faculty may become candidates for graduate degrees with approval from the academic program, the university employer, and the Graduate School. To receive approval, candidates must address conflicts of interest, time, and commitment. Supervisors of these candidates should abstain from chairing and/or serving on the candidates' graduate committees to avoid potential conflicts of interest.
The Conflict of Interest Mitigation in Graduate School form and guidelines for staff and administrative/professional faculty seeking a graduate degree may be found at https://graduateschool.vt.edu/academics/expectations/COI.html.
Questions may be directed to Associate Dean Bill Huckle (wrhuckle@vt.edu).
Once completed, the form and appropriate attachments must be uploaded in the Graduate School's Form Submission Portal.
